intro:
Use it for a task that belongs to the page but should not leave it: answering an invitation, editing a profile, changing a setting. It rises from an edge, stands a few pixels clear of every side with its corners rounded, and goes back with a swipe, the Escape key or a click outside.

A sheet that needs the whole height can meet the edges instead: set `size="full"` or `detached={false}`.

A sheet can open another. Declare the second one inside the first as `Sheet.Next` with a `name`, and any `Sheet.Trigger to="name"` in the first opens it: a row in the body, an icon in the header, a button in the footer. The first sheet steps back behind it. Wrap the app in `Sheet.Stage` and the page steps back too.

For a decision that needs an answer before anything else, use a dialog. For one question with a written answer, use [Feedback](/docs/web/components/feedback).
usage:
<Sheet>
  <Sheet.Trigger render={<Button />}>Edit profile</Sheet.Trigger>
  <Sheet.Content>
    <Sheet.Header title="Edit profile" description="Shown on your public page." />
    <Sheet.Body>
      <Field>
        <FieldLabel>Name</FieldLabel>
        <Input defaultValue="Noor Haddad" />
      </Field>
    </Sheet.Body>
    <Sheet.Footer>
      <Sheet.Close render={<Button />}>Save changes</Sheet.Close>
      <Sheet.Close render={<Button variant="ghost" />}>Cancel</Sheet.Close>
    </Sheet.Footer>
  </Sheet.Content>
</Sheet>

parts.Trigger: What opens a sheet. A plain button, or your own through `render`. With `to`, it opens the `Sheet.Next` of that name instead, and `payload` is handed to that sheet.
parts.Content: The sheet and the backdrop behind it. It draws the grabber on a top or bottom sheet and the round close button in the top trailing corner. `showGrabber={false}` and `showClose={false}` leave them out. `inline` draws it in the page instead of over it.
parts.Next: A second sheet, opened from the first by any `Sheet.Trigger` whose `to` is its `name`. Declare it anywhere inside the first sheet's content. It takes the same props as `Content` and draws its own, so its children are the header, body and footer. Pass a function as its children to read the opening trigger's `payload`.
parts.Header: The title and a line under it, as `title` and `description` or as `Title` and `Description` children. It leaves room for the close button on the same line.
parts.Title: The sheet's name. It is also what a screen reader announces when the sheet opens.
parts.Description: A sentence under the title, read out after it.
parts.Body: The part that scrolls. The header and footer stay where they are while it moves.
parts.Slides: A column of rounded slides in place of `Sheet.Body`, for photos or a deck. By default it is a deck: each slide fills the sheet's height, a scroll glides to the next slide, the arrow keys move one at a time, and a counter sits under it. `snap={false}` makes it a numbered column of smaller slides that scrolls freely, and with `onIndexChange` pressing one chooses it. `index` and `defaultIndex` hold the current slide.
parts.Slide: One slide: a rounded frame that an image or a video fills edge to edge, or anything drawn. `label` is what a screen reader calls it after its place, such as "3 of 8".
parts.Close: Closes the sheet, even when `dismissible` is off. Give it `render` or children to make your own button close it. Written with nothing inside, it is the round close button, drawn where it is written; the one in the corner is then left out. Inside `Sheet.Header` it shares the title's line, before the title or after it depending on where it is written.
parts.Stage: Wraps the page. While a sheet inside it is open, the page steps back slightly and rounds its corners. Set `--stage-radius` to the radius of what it sits in, less the gap, so the two corners are concentric.

examples.title: From any edge
examples.description: `side` sets the edge the sheet rises from and is swiped back to. Side sheets run the full height, still clear of the edges.

examples.title: Text you can copy
examples.description: With a mouse, the title, description, body and footer are for reading: a double-click selects a word and a drag selects a line, the same as on the page. Drag the sheet by its grabber or the space around the header. On a touch screen a finger still swipes the sheet from anywhere.

examples.title: Your own close button
examples.description: Write a bare `<Sheet.Close />` where the close button should go. Here it is first in `Sheet.Header`, so it stands before the title on the same line, and the sheet leaves its corner empty.

examples.title: Without a close button
examples.description: `showClose={false}` removes the close button. With `dismissible={false}` as well, the only way out is a `Sheet.Close` in the footer, which suits a sheet that needs an answer before the task can go on.

examples.title: Photos, one at a time
examples.description: `Sheet.Slides` in a `size="full"` sheet is a deck of rounded slides, each as tall as the sheet. A turn of the wheel or a swipe of the trackpad glides to the next photo, however hard it is, and on a touch screen the photo follows the finger and settles. The arrow keys move one at a time, and the counter under it says which one is showing.

examples.title: A deck in a column
examples.description: With `snap={false}` the slides become a numbered column that scrolls freely, like a presentation's slide panel. Given `onIndexChange`, each slide is a button: pressing one chooses it and rings it in the info colour, and the arrow keys move the choice. `index` holds the choice outside, to show the slide wherever the page needs it.

examples.title: A sheet from a sheet
examples.description: Declare the second sheet as `Sheet.Next` inside the first, and give a `Sheet.Trigger` in the first its `name` as `to`. The trigger can be anything in the sheet. Here it is each row of a list, made pressable by `render`. The second sheet slides over from the same edge, and the first one steps back: a little smaller, pushed inward, and faded. Only the first sheet darkens the page.

examples.title: One sheet for every row
examples.description: A trigger's `payload` reaches the `Sheet.Next` it opens. Give the sheet a function as its children and it is called with the payload, so one declaration serves every row of a list.

examples.title: From the header
examples.description: A trigger in the header, beside the title, for an action on the whole sheet's subject.

examples.title: Three deep
examples.description: A `Sheet.Next` can hold its own `Sheet.Next`. Here an item opens from the order, and removing it asks first, in a third sheet. Each sheet behind the front one steps back a little further.

examples.title: A sheet from a sheet, from any edge
examples.description: Stacking works from every side. A `Sheet.Next` rises from the edge of the sheet it is declared in unless it is given a `side`. The sheet behind is pushed inward from its own edge, so a strip of it still shows.

examples.title: The page steps back
examples.description: Everything inside `Sheet.Stage` steps back slightly while a sheet is open, so the sheet sits on a layer above the page. Here the stage sits in a frame with 32px corners, so `--stage-radius` is 26px.

notes:
### Closing a stack

A press outside the sheets closes all of them. Escape, a swipe and `Sheet.Close` close only the one on top, and the one behind it comes forward again.

### Names

A `Sheet.Next` name is shared by every sheet in one stack, so a trigger finds its sheet however deep either of them is. Use each name once per stack.

A sheet written as a plain `<Sheet>` inside another sheet's content also stacks. That needs its trigger wrapped in it, so use `Sheet.Next` when the trigger and the sheet are apart.

### Gestures

Swiping follows the pointer, and a quick flick toward the edge closes the sheet even when it has not moved far.

With a mouse, a press on text selects it instead of starting a drag. The grabber and the padding around the header still drag the sheet. Touch swipes from anywhere, except while text in the sheet is selected.

`dismissible={false}` keeps a click outside, Escape and a swipe from closing it. Only `Sheet.Close` and your own `open` state close it then.

`size` applies to top and bottom sheets. Side sheets always run the full height.

Focus moves into the sheet when it opens and returns to the trigger when it closes. The page behind cannot be scrolled or focused while it is open.

With reduced motion turned on, the sheet appears and disappears without sliding.

### Slides need a height

A deck fills the height it is given, so put it in a sheet that has one: a side sheet, or a top or bottom sheet with `size="half"` or `size="full"`. In a sheet that sizes itself to its content it falls back to 60% of the screen, at most 32rem. A column needs no height of its own; it scrolls once it reaches the edge of the screen.
